dataSetInformation.common:generalComment:
This dataset represents the Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) of the cradle-to-gate production of 1 kg of container glass from primary materials, including (but not limited to) raw material extraction, transport, glass bottle production, ancillary products, internal recycling activities and process waste treatment. This dataset is based on the critical reviewed LCA study ("Life Cycle Assessment of Container Glass in Europe") carried out by RDC Environment, commissioned by the European Container Glass Federation (FEVE) and completed in December 2016. In order to deliver the current LCI, the original LCA model of FEVE study was updated by modifying: the background database from Ecoinvent 2.2 to Ecoinvent 3.5; the energy and transport processes to be EF-compliant; by applying the Circular Footprint Formula CFF (“20:80”). The list of elementary flows was updated to be aligned with the EF package v3.0 provided by the EC. This dataset represents a theoretical container glass made of 60% virgin raw materials and 40% recycled content (R1) or cullet content; the model is extrapolated from real data of the container glass industry by calculating the melting energy at the furnace as function of the external cullet content in the batch. Average distances from glass manufacturing site to fillers are:
- Road transport: 0.35 t*km by articulated lorry 28-32 tons EURO 4 norm - Rail transport: 3.32304E-5 t*km by freight train electric traction - Rail transport: 5.4096E-6 t*km by freight train diesel traction - Boat transport: 8.700937E-2 t*km by transoceanic container ship

time.common:timeRepresentativenessDescription: Primary data of container glass production (bottles and jars) were collected for the year 2012, which was a standard year for container glass manufacturing. As no breakthrough of technological evolution of the container glass manufacturing is foreseen in the incoming years, the time validity of this study is 3 – 5 years.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Raw material production and transport, fossil fuels production (except natural gas) and distribution were modelled to reflect the average European scenario, while electricity generation and natural gas production and distribution were modelled to reflect country specific scenario.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: All common types of furnace technology and colours of container glass (amber, green, flint and other colour) are covered. Site-specific data for FEVE LCA study were collected among 219 furnaces and 7 cullet treatment plants, covering 84% of the European sold volume for the year 2012 and equivalent to 17.5 million tons of sold container glass.

LCIMethodAndAllocation.deviationsFromLCIMethodApproaches:
Allocation of inputs and outputs at the container glass manufacturing site: all the inputs and outputs occurring at the container glass manufacturing sites have been allocated based on mass criteria. End-of-Life allocation of the container glass recycling: 20-80 allocation with CFF formula.
Co-product allocation of the export of heat surplus from furnaces or waste incineration: modelled as substituting the corresponding heat mix.
As regards background datasets, most of the datasets used in the study apply allocation rules. No change was made to these allocation rules, which are thus following the general approach of Ecoinvent v3.3 cut-off allocation and GaBi v5 databases.
LCIMethodAndAllocation.modellingConstants:
Recycled content (R1) or cullet content: 40%
Quality factor applied to secondary material (Qs/Qp): 1
Energy saving in the container glass furnace thanks to the use of external cullet: 2.8% energy saving for each 10% external cullet used in the batch. Carbon storage and delayed emissions: credits associated with temporary (carbon) storage or delayed emissions are not considered in the calculation of the EF for the default impact categories. Emissions off-setting: not included

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples:
A cut-off rule based on mass or energy flow or the level of environmental significance of max. 3% is applied and confirmed by the reviewer. An active cut-off within the system has not been applied, no data gaps are known and all elementary flows of environmental effect are included in the inventory.
Capital goods (including infrastructures) and their end of life are included unless the exclusion is clearly documented and conform with the cut-off principles.
System boundaries include all known processes linked to the product supply chain.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.deviationsFromCutOffAndCompletenessPrinc:
The processes excluded according to the cut-off criteria are: Production of the raw materials with very small share of the batch composition.
Maintenance and operation of support equipment.
Furnace rebuilding.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataSelectionAndCombinationPrinciples: Primary data of container glass production (bottles and jars) were collected for the year 2012 from 219 furnaces and 7 cullet treatment plants. This covers more than 17.5 million tons of sold container glass or 84% of the European sold volume for the year 2012. Background datasets used to model upstream raw material and fossil fuel production and transport refers to European average technologies. Background datasets come from Ecoinvent v3.3 or GaBi v5 databases. Energy and transport data came from the LCDN node.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataTreatmentAndExtrapolationsPrinciples: A horizontal averaging approach was performed to average data across the 219 container glass manufacturing plants. The horizontal averaging approach consists in weighting each collected primary data (e.g., amount of silica sand, amount of natural gas, etc.) according to the sales volume of the plant, and then averaging them in order to produce a virtual plant. The LCIs and LCIA are then calculated based on the virtual average plant. This approach was used in the study because it is the best compromise between quality of the results and time and resource availability. This dataset represents a theoretical container glass made of 60% virgin raw materials and 40% recycled content (R1) or cullet content; the model is extrapolated from real data of the container glass industry by calculating the melting energy at the furnace as function of the external cullet content in the batch. Energy saving in the container glass furnace thanks to the use of external cullet: 2.8% energy saving for each 10% external cullet used in the batch.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.useAdviceForDataSet: Notice: this data set supersedes the EF3.0-compliant version (see link under "preceding data set version" below calculated with the EF3.0). The life cycle inventory is not changed from the original EF3.0 data set. The LCIA results are calculated based on the EF3.1 methods which provide updated characterisation factors in the following impact categories: Climate Change, Ecotoxicity freshwater, Photochemical Ozone Formation, Acidification, Human Toxicity non-cancer, and Human Toxicity cancer. The review report and the data quality ratings refer to the original results. The data set has been updated by the European Commission on the basis of the original EF3.0 data set delivered by the data provider. Life Cycle Inventory (LCI) datasets to be used for implementing regular Product Environmental Footprint (PEF) studies and Organisation Environmental Footprint (OEF) studies exclusively under the specified Product groups and sectors as defined in the Product Environmental Footprint Category Rules (PEFCR) and Organisation Environmental Footprint Sectorial Rules (OEFSR) listed in http://ec.eiirona.eu/enviiOnment/eussd/smgp/PEFCR OEFSR en.htm and in accordance with the terms and conditions of this EULA exclusively until 31st December 2024 (PERMITTED USE). The datasets are specifically designed for these methodological requirements (see above) and the related LCIA methods (listed below) recommended in EF.

review.common:reviewDetails:
The data set achieves an overall DQR of good (2.0), applying the DQR rules of the related PEFCR guidance. The data set meets the requirements for an EF compliant data set, as specified in the referenced documents of the compliant system, i.e. PEFCR guidance, and the applicable PEFCR.
This dataset has the following DQRs: Technological representativeness: good (2.0) Time representativeness: good (2.0) Geographical representativeness: good (2.0) Precision: good (2.0) Good overall quality (2.0)
review.common:otherReviewDetails: The review procedure concerning EF 3.0 data is to be understood as additional review on top of the already existing independent panel review for EF 2.0, as far as updates are concerned. The review was undertaken as independent internal review for the update from EF 2.0 to EF 3.0; done by Peter Shonfield and Manfred Russ. Please see related EF 3.0 review details: http://www.gabi-software.com/fileadmin/GaBi_Databases/Internal_Review_Statement_for_EF_3-0.pdf
